PullRequest.Title: Persist full Codex command output across chat reloads
PullRequest.Body:
Part of: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/328596
Follow-up to: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/335016

- Keep Codex command output of up to 80,000 characters inline and unchanged.
- Store larger output in the owning chat's session database, within the existing 10 MiB limit, and show its first 400 characters unchanged with **Open Full Output (Read-Only)**. Completed output is served from the database; no terminal is kept alive.
- Use the stable Codex item id as the tool-call id live and on replay. Coalesced sandbox pre-flights keep the pre-flight id, matching the live mapper.
- Queue retained-output storage before both ordinary `item/completed` actions and command completions recovered from `turn/completed`, without changing turn or notification ordering.
- Restore retained terminal resources on the initial history read and when changed native turns replace incremental observed history.
- Remove retained output when `thread/revert` or `thread/rollback` removes its turn. Session deletion removes the remaining database.
- Treat Codex command executions as OS-shell-neutral. Bash/zsh `-c` and PowerShell/pwsh `-Command` wrappers are removed only for display; retention keeps the raw item identity and output.
- Leave output over 10 MiB, Codex subagent commands, and output that the database did not retain unchanged.


### Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npm run test-node -- --runGlob "**/agentHost/test/{node,common}/**/*.test.js"` — 8,145 passing
- ESLint on the changed files
- `turn completion recovery retains large parent output but leaves subagent output inline`
- `observed history refresh preserves retained command output on changed turns`

### Manual verification

In a Codex chat, run:

```text
printf 'FULL_OUTPUT_BEGIN\n'; head -c 131072 /dev/zero | tr '\0' x; printf '\nFULL_OUTPUT_MIDDLE\n'; head -c 131072 /dev/zero | tr '\0' y; printf '\nFULL_OUTPUT_END\n'
```

Verify that:

- the card starts with `FULL_OUTPUT_BEGIN` and the raw beginning of the `x` output;
- the card shows the truncation message and **Open Full Output (Read-Only)**;
- the read-only editor contains the beginning, middle, and end markers;
- after restarting the Agent Host and reloading the window, the same card still opens the full output;
- output under 80,000 characters, such as `seq 1 3000`, has no truncation message or full-output action.

On Windows or anywhere `pwsh` is available, repeat with:

```text
$x = 'x' * 131072; $y = 'y' * 131072; [Console]::Out.Write("FULL_OUTPUT_BEGIN`n$x`nFULL_OUTPUT_MIDDLE`n$y`nFULL_OUTPUT_END`n")
```

Verify that the card displays the script rather than the `powershell.exe`/`pwsh -Command` wrapper, with the same retention and restore behavior.

-----------------------------------------
Inspirations from:

- Storing complete output in the chat's session database follows Copilot's capture in [`CopilotAgentSession`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/4212437dd11e9c7e728caa26a269540c87343930/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgentSession.ts#L5960-L5983) from #335016.
- Restoring retained resources on history reconstruction mirrors [`_restoreStoredShellOutputsForChat`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/4212437dd11e9c7e728caa26a269540c87343930/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgentSession.ts#L3745-L3771).
- Serving completed output without a live terminal relies on [`AgentService._resolveRetainedTerminalState`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/4212437dd11e9c7e728caa26a269540c87343930/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentService.ts#L5834-L5898).
- Write-before-publish ordering relies on [`storeTerminalOutput`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/4212437dd11e9c7e728caa26a269540c87343930/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/sessionDatabase.ts#L918-L937) and [`readTerminalOutput`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/4212437dd11e9c7e728caa26a269540c87343930/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/sessionDatabase.ts#L952-L965) sharing the [turn-data sequencer](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/4212437dd11e9c7e728caa26a269540c87343930/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/sessionDatabase.ts#L426-L432).
- The 80,000-character inline limit reuses [`SHELL_COMMAND_MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/4212437dd11e9c7e728caa26a269540c87343930/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/shared/shellCommandExecution.ts#L14-L18).
- Rollback cleanup corresponds to Copilot pruning database turns on [truncation](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/4212437dd11e9c7e728caa26a269540c87343930/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgentSession.ts#L7804-L7810).

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The synchronous call order, unbounded accumulated string, allocation, and post-allocation rejection are directly visible in the changed call path. Exact stall duration depends on output size and machine memory, but the mechanism and linear scaling are certain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: CPU work and a UTF-8 buffer proportional to the complete command output
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The synchronous encoding and temporary allocation grow linearly with the command's full output size, with no bound before encoding; outputs above 10 MiB pay the entire cost and are then discarded.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: blocked agent-host event loop, delayed command completion publication, and memory/GC pressure for very large command output
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Command completion reused the already-accumulated output string and published it directly; it did not synchronously create a second full UTF-8 representation before mapping the completion.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every output above the 80,000-character retention threshold is synchronously converted with VSBuffer.fromString before the 10 MiB database limit is checked, including output that can never be retained.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added RIGHT line 3633 performs `VSBuffer.fromString(output)` before added RIGHT line 3634 rejects `content.byteLength > MAX_TERMINAL_OUTPUT_BYTES`; this full-output encoding did not exist before the PR.
Findings.Title: Reject oversized output before encoding it
Findings.Impact: A command that prints a large log or file (for example, tens or hundreds of MiB) now blocks all agent-host notification processing while allocating another full copy, only to reject it afterward; completion and other chats can visibly stall and the extra allocation can trigger heavy GC or OOM pressure.
Findings.Evidence: _dispatchItemCompleted calls _retainCommandOutput synchronously before firing ChatToolCallComplete. The changed line invokes VSBuffer.fromString(output), while the next line is the first MAX_TERMINAL_OUTPUT_BYTES check. Codex output is accumulated without a size cap in mapCommandExecutionOutputDelta via `entry.output += params.delta`, so the input to this conversion is not bounded by the database limit.
Findings.Recommendation: Check `output.length > MAX_TERMINAL_OUTPUT_BYTES` before any encoding (UTF-8 cannot be shorter than the JS code-unit count), then use a non-allocating byte-length check for remaining multibyte cases and only create the VSBuffer for output that will actually be stored.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed loop cardinality, awaited call path, SQL operation, and sequencer-enforced serialization are explicit. The exact delay varies by chat length and storage speed, which affects severity but not the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: serialized SQLite DELETE mutations and their filesystem transaction work
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The awaited rollback cost grows with every commandExecution in the removed turn suffix, not with the smaller set of commands that actually retained output; N commands produce N serialized database mutations.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased rollback latency and excessive database/filesystem I/O on long chats
Findings.PreviousBehavior: After the single app-server thread/revert or thread/rollback request completed, truncateChat returned without issuing per-command SQLite mutations.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new cleanup collects every removed command id and awaits Promise.all of deleteTerminalOutput calls. SessionDatabase routes each call through one turn-usage sequencer and a separate SQLite DELETE, so the apparent Promise.all is effectively N serial mutations.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added RIGHT line 6545 fans the removed command-id collection into one awaited `deleteTerminalOutput` call per command; before this diff no local deletion boundary existed on truncateChat.
Findings.Title: Batch retained-output deletion for reverted turns
Findings.Impact: Reverting a long Codex chat with hundreds of shell commands now waits for hundreds of separate SQLite DELETE operations—even when most commands had inline output and no row to delete—delaying completion of the user’s rollback action.
Findings.Evidence: _deleteRetainedCommandOutputs builds toolCallIds from all commandExecution items, then the changed line invokes deleteTerminalOutput once per id. sessionDatabase.ts implements deleteTerminalOutput as one `DELETE FROM terminal_outputs WHERE tool_call_id = ?` through `_mutateTurnUsage`; that helper serializes all operations on `_turnUsageSequencer`. truncateChat awaits this helper after the remote revert, placing all mutations on its critical path.
Findings.Recommendation: Add a bounded bulk database operation that deletes all supplied tool-call ids in one transaction/statement (or deletes retained outputs by the reverted turn ids), and await that single cleanup operation after the app-server rollback.

Scenarios.Scenario: A parent Codex command completes with large output during an active chat
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The item/completed handler synchronously selects the full output, checks the 80,000-character retention threshold, encodes it with VSBuffer.fromString, checks the 10 MiB storage cap, maps the completion, and publishes it. UTF-8 encoding is on the critical path; the SQLite store is queued before publication but completes off the publication critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Encode the complete JavaScript output string into a UTF-8 VSBuffer
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per parent command output above 80,000 characters, including rejected output above 10 MiB
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The existing output string was passed through to completion mapping without creating a second full UTF-8 representation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous and blocks completion publication and the agent-host event loop

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Store accepted complete output in terminal_outputs
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One queued write per qualifying command at or below 10 MiB
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Codex command completion did not persist output in the session database.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Queued before publication for ordering but not awaited by completion publication; later reads serialize behind it

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The command's complete output size. One retention attempt occurs per parent command whose output exceeds 80,000 characters; outputs above 10 MiB are not stored but are still fully encoded.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Item notifications execute serially on the agent-host event loop. Accepted database writes are serialized with other turn-data operations by the session database sequencer; separate commands may queue multiple writes but do not execute them concurrently within one database.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No output-size or encoding cache exists. Every qualifying completion performs the check and encoding once. Database/open-reference reuse may make warm storage access cheaper, but it does not avoid serialization.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the changed code performs full synchronous encoding before its only 10 MiB rejection, while command deltas accumulate without a cap.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact event-loop stall and GC cost depend on output size and host memory; commands printing tens or hundreds of MiB are realistic, and no protocol-side bound was found.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable high-severity serialization/allocation regression because rejected oversized output incurs unbounded synchronous work and allocation.

Scenarios.Scenario: A command completion is recovered only from turn/completed
Scenarios.CriticalPath: _handleTurnCompletedNotification scans unresolved command items, and each qualifying parent command follows the same synchronous retention/encoding path before mapTurnCompleted returns actions. Storage remains queued rather than awaited.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Encode each recovered qualifying command's complete output
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per unresolved large parent command in the recovered turn
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Recovered command output was mapped inline without retention encoding.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One write per accepted recovered output
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No recovered Codex output write occurred.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Write completion is off the immediate action-publication path, though ordering is enforced for later reads

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number and byte size of unresolved command executions present in the completed turn; effective cardinality excludes commands already removed from itemToToolCall and excludes subagent recovery.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The recovery loop is synchronous and serial. Accepted SQLite writes are queued on the database turn-data sequencer.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache; each unresolved qualifying command is independently encoded and considered for storage.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the recovery loop directly invokes the same changed retention helper.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Recovery is less frequent than ordinary item completion and usually has few unresolved commands, but output size remains unbounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: Covered by the same reported pre-cap encoding finding; no separate duplicate finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or reload a Codex chat and reconstruct retained command output
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing thread/read and paginated thread/turns/list app-server requests hydrate full history, replay maps turns, then the new restore step opens the session database and serially probes getTerminalOutputSize for each replayed command over 80,000 characters before getMessages returns.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read thread metadata and full turn pages from the Codex app server
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing one metadata request plus one or more 100-turn pages for paginated history
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same full-history app-server reads already occurred.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before history mapping; not introduced or moved by this diff

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open the chat session database and query terminal output existence/size by tool-call id
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One open and one serialized SELECT per replayed command candidate over 80,000 characters
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Replay returned mapped history without consulting the session database for Codex command output.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before initial chat messages are returned

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of replayed shell commands with output above 80,000 characters after sandbox pre-flight coalescing; one probe per effective displayed command candidate.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: App-server history pages are requested serially. Database size probes are also awaited serially and the database itself sequences turn-data operations.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold opens incur database initialization and queries; warm OS/database state can reduce latency. There is no retained-id cache. Watched refreshes limit replay/probes to changed turns, while initial reads inspect all candidates.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the added serial probes and critical-path placement; lower for material user-visible magnitude relative to existing history hydration.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Long histories can contain many candidates, but full-history network transfer and parsing already scale with the same large outputs, and the query pattern mirrors the existing Copilot restoration design; evidence was insufficient for a separate high-confidence regression finding.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: concrete extra work exists, but available evidence does not establish material impact beyond the already scaling history load.

Scenarios.Scenario: A watched Codex chat history refresh replaces changed native turns
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing history watcher reads changed app-server history; changed turns are replayed, then retained-output database probes complete before the refreshed history event is published.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh thread history from the Codex app server
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing paginated requests until the previous-history anchor is reached
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Watcher already refreshed native thread history.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Precedes changed-turn detection and was already on the refresh path

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Probe retained terminal output size for changed large command calls
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One serialized SELECT per large command in changed turns
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Changed turns were mapped and published without database probes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Large command outputs in turns detected as changed since the previous raw snapshot, not the entire unchanged history.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Refreshes are globally queued through _chatHistoryReads. Candidate database probes are serial within a refresh.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Previous raw and mapped turn snapshots avoid replaying and probing unchanged turns. There is no cache for retained-output existence on changed turns.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for placement and cardinality, moderate for material latency.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Changed-turn filtering generally keeps cardinality low; pathological replacement of many turns is possible but not shown as common.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding because snapshot filtering bounds normal refresh work and material impact is not sufficiently evidenced.

Scenarios.Scenario: Revert or roll back a suffix of a Codex chat
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing app-server thread/revert or thread/rollback request completes first. The new cleanup then opens the chat database and awaits deletion for every command execution in all removed turns before truncateChat resolves.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Revert or roll back the Codex app-server thread
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: truncateChat resolved after this app-server request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing awaited boundary before local cleanup

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Delete terminal output by individual command tool-call id
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One serialized SQLite DELETE for every removed command, not merely every retained output
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No local database cleanup operations ran on the rollback path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All deletes are awaited before rollback completion

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Total commandExecution items in the removed turn suffix, including commands with inline, empty, over-limit, or otherwise unretained output.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Promise.all creates all requests, but deleteTerminalOutput routes every mutation through the single _turnUsageSequencer; effective SQLite concurrency is one, with a separate DELETE mutation per command.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No retained-id filtering or negative cache exists. Missing terminal-output rows still execute DELETE statements. Warm database state does not remove per-command SQL/transaction overhead.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: collection construction, awaited fan-out, SQL implementation, and sequencer serialization are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact latency depends on removed history length and filesystem speed; long agent chats can realistically contain hundreds of shell commands.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity boundary fan-out regression; cleanup should be bulked into one database operation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Replay shell command identity and unwrap Bash/PowerShell display wrappers
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Pure in-memory replay and regular-expression/string processing produce stable tool-call ids and display command text. No subprocess is launched and no command is re-executed.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of replayed command items and command-line string length.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous per replayed item; no queue or external concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache, but work is bounded to one regex/string pass per command during existing mapping.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that these changes are pure in-memory mapping.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Command-line strings are normally small; no evidence of a hot per-frame path or materially expensive inputs.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across all 12 changed files. Submitted two findings: unbounded synchronous UTF-8 encoding before the 10 MiB cap, and serialized per-command SQLite cleanup on rollback. Examined live/recovered completion, initial replay, watched refresh, rollback cleanup, replay identity, shell display mapping, storage ordering, cache behavior, and effective database concurrency; no concrete shipped-regression fix warranted blame/report_regression_fix.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
